newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain labour talks stuck on youth contracts.
newsitem.headline: Spain labour talks stuck on youth contracts.

text.p: Spain's labour reform talks between employers and unions have become stuck on the key issue of contracts for youths, unions said on Thursday.
Employers and unions were aware that negotiations still faced a number of difficulties but were optimistic that an accord would eventually be reached.
"We are very much committed to reaching an accord that will bring more stability to employment," Candido Mendez, Secretary General of the General Workers' Union (UGT) told a news conference.
Earlier employers accused unions of slowing the talks with their latest proposal on the hiring of young people.
The two have been in intensive talks for three days, after having started negotiations to reduce Europe's highest unemployment rate in January.
But unions fiercely denied this and said employers were simply suffering from "an attack of nerves".

"The unions have not introduced any slowdown in the talks; it is just that employers are not moving their position," Antonio Gutierrez, Secretary General of the Workers Commission union (CCOO) told reporters.
Unions are proposing a two- to four-year youth temporary contract that would be converted automatically into a permanent contract upon expiry.
Employers, meanwhile, want the temporary youth contract to terminate after 10 years without any redundacy payment.
The government has given unions and employers until early March to reach an agreement before it steps in and imposes a package of reforms.
Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said earlier on Thursday he was confident the two sides would reach an accord.
